name: dropdown-picker
summary: The product's custom select: popover-anchored, virtualized, searchable, single/multi-select, keyboard nav, optional inline-add. Not a native/Ant select.

variants.name: tree-select
variants.what: hierarchical expand/collapse tree in the menu

variants.name: column-chooser
variants.what: table show/hide-columns dropdown: COLUMNS header + draggable checkbox rows + Reset footer (column-selector.vue, 174×)

optionShape.label: text || name || label
extra: avatar (URL → img, else initials from label) + sublabel/email (people picker)

value.note: v-model; key (single) or array of keys (multiple)

asInput.note: defaults TRUE (F3); trigger looks like an input. LEGACY — prefer the `trigger` enum.

trigger.note: [element] trigger style: input (default) | text | button | icon | chip. One enum consolidating asInput/textOnly + adding button + icon. Orthogonal to the menu content.

triggerIcon.note: [element] the glyph (obs-icon name) for the `icon` trigger (default ellipsisV) and the leading caret of the `button` trigger (default chevronDown).

triggerLabel.note: [element] a fixed label for the button/icon trigger (e.g. "Columns", "Filter") instead of the selection/placeholder.

maxValues.note: the REAL selection cap (sliced in handleChange)

maxAllowedSelection.note: DEAD — declared but never used (F2); use maxValues

columns.note: COLUMN-CHOOSER mode — a JSON array of {key,label,checked?,locked?}. Renders a heading + draggable checkbox rows (drag-reorder; a locked column is pinned) instead of the option list. Opens from an eye icon trigger by default. Emits change/reorder/reset.

heading.note: (column-chooser) the section header at the top of the menu, e.g. "COLUMNS".

reset-label.note: (column-chooser) the reset-footer text, e.g. "Reset Column Preference" (undo icon). Omit for no footer.

triggers.note: The trigger slot ({ toggle }) controls HOW the dropdown opens — orthogonal to the menu content. Any menu variant can use any trigger.

input.useWhen: a form field — the standard bordered box with the selection + chevron

text-only.useWhen: inline / embedded in a sentence or compact header — plain text + caret, no box

button.useWhen: the opener reads as an ACTION with a label

icon-only.useWhen: a compact toolbar / row where space is tight — an icon button (kebab / gear / filter)
icon-only.example: row kebab menus, toolbar option buttons

chip.useWhen: a compact token-like opener, often in a filter bar
chip.example: filter chips that open a value menu

accessibility.keyboardOpen: ArrowUp/Down/Enter/Escape work only once open (window keydown)
accessibility.gaps: F1 — no combobox ARIA, not keyboard-openable (click-only), no focus ring (SF-001)

do: Use as the standard select; options as { key, text }; v-model the key(s).
multiple + allow-select-all for multi; :searchable=false for short lists; trigger slot for custom triggers.
dont: Don't rely on maxAllowedSelection to cap (F2 — use maxValues).
Don't assume keyboard/AT users can operate it today (F1). Don't forget searchable/asInput/wrap default true (F3).
whenToUse: The default select control anywhere in the product (single or multi).
decisionFlow: Free-form typed tags? -> LooseTags, not the picker.

Picking a rich RECORD identified by MULTIPLE columns (name/IP/type/status), often multi-select with checkboxes? -> Grid Select (obs-grid-select), not this — its menu is a searchable TABLE, not an option list.
Choosing one/many from a simple {label} list? -> DropdownPicker.
User can add missing options? -> can-user-add-options + add-label.

Options need a VISUAL cue to identify them (a status/severity dot, a type icon, a person's avatar)? -> [element] give each option `severity`/`icon`/`avatar`+`sublabel` (OPTION CONTENT — one rich option schema, NOT a separate component).
Options are HIERARCHICAL (parent/child, e.g. DC > Rack > Server)? -> [element] give options nested `children[]` (tree-select: expand/collapse, branch = subtree select).

How should it OPEN (orthogonal to the above)? -> [element] the `trigger` enum: input (default form field) | text (inline) | button (labelled action, e.g. Columns/Filter) | icon (compact toolbar/kebab/filter, with a count badge) | chip (filter-bar token).
Showing/hiding (and reordering) a TABLE’s columns? -> this Dropdown with a `columns` prop (the column-chooser mode: COLUMNS header + draggable checkbox rows + Reset).

single(default).useWhen: pick one value from a list (most common)

multiple.useWhen: pick several values (checkboxes + Select-All + Clear); add allow-select-all

searchable=false.useWhen: short fixed list where search is noise (119x)

allow-clear.useWhen: an empty/none state is valid and resettable (218x)

as-input.useWhen: trigger should look like a form field (default true); false for chip/inline trigger

can-user-add-options.useWhen: user may need a value not in the list (inline add -> emits add)

trigger-slot.useWhen: default input trigger doesn't fit (button, avatar, pills)

cap-selection.useWhen: limit count -> use maxValues, NOT maxAllowedSelection (dead, F2)

single.useWhen: Pick exactly one value from a list — the default and most common mode. Options are { key, text } and v-model binds the selected key. Trigger looks like a form field (asInput) unless overridden.
single.dontUse: Don't use for choosing several values (use `multiple`), for free-form typed tags (use LooseTags), or for 2-3 always-visible exclusive options (use MRadio segmented) or a simple on/off (MSwitch).
single.example: Choosing a monitor type, a template, or an owner; the severity picker; entity pickers like monitor-picker / user-picker / group-picker.

not-searchable.useWhen: The list is short and fixed (≤ ~7 items) so the search box would just be noise — set `:searchable="false"` (search defaults TRUE). Used 119×.
not-searchable.dontUse: Don't disable search on long or dynamic lists where the user needs to filter — keep the default searchable behaviour there.
not-searchable.example: A short fixed enum select such as a status or a small fixed set of options where scanning is faster than typing.

text-only.useWhen: The trigger should be plain text rather than a form-field-looking input — set `textOnly` (asInput off). A lightweight, inline-looking trigger. Used 15×.
text-only.dontUse: Don't use where the control should read as an editable form field (that's the default `asInput` input trigger). For fully custom triggers (button/avatar/pills) use the `trigger` slot instead.
text-only.example: An inline, label-style select embedded in dense text or a toolbar where a boxed input would be visually heavy.

read-only-pills.useWhen: A multi-select is disabled/read-only and you want to display the chosen values as teal SelectedItemPills instead of an editable trigger — the `multiple` + `disabled` presentation.
read-only-pills.dontUse: Don't use when the user still needs to edit the selection (keep the enabled `multiple` trigger). For an editable single value, use `single`.
read-only-pills.example: Monitoring Hours shown in a read-only/disabled state renders the selected hours as SelectedItemPills; any disabled multi-select summary.

inline-add.useWhen: The user may need a value that isn't in the list yet — set `can-user-add-options` (+ `add-label`) to expose an inline add action in the search area that emits `add`.
inline-add.dontUse: Don't use for a closed/fixed set of options, or for truly free-form typed tags (use LooseTags for that).
inline-add.example: Pickers where the user can create a missing option on the fly (e.g. adding a tag/label that doesn't exist yet) and have it emitted via `add`.

two-pane.useWhen: Options need explanatory context — set `useAfterMenuDescription` to render a two-pane layout: the option menu plus a description panel for the hovered item.
two-pane.dontUse: Don't use for simple lists where labels are self-explanatory; the extra description pane is wasted space there.
two-pane.example: A picker where each option needs a hovered-item description to disambiguate choices (e.g. selecting among options whose meaning isn't obvious from the label alone).

use-popover.useWhen: Anchor the dropdown with the kit's `MPopover` instead of the default `MPopper` (v-tooltip) — set `usePopover`. Used 26× where the MPopover overlay/positioning behaviour is needed.
use-popover.dontUse: Don't switch off the default unless you specifically need MPopover semantics; the standard trigger uses MPopper by default.
use-popover.example: Pickers embedded in contexts that already rely on the MPopover overlay kit for consistent positioning/stacking.

grid-dropdown (table picker).useWhen: The user picks from RICH RECORDS where each row needs multiple columns to identify it — name + IP + type + status — and often multi-select with checkboxes. The menu is a searchable TABLE, not a plain option list.
grid-dropdown (table picker).dontUse: Not for simple {label} options (use the plain dropdown) or a short fixed list. Not for a menu of ACTIONS (that is a Menu / _base-grid-actions, not a picker).
grid-dropdown (table picker).example: Select Agent / Select Monitor pickers (~70×): agent, monitor, device, interface, RUM service, integration/SNMP-trap profile, and user selection. Generic base = FlotoDropdownGridSelector (pass your own columns + rows); the monitor/agent variant adds async server-search + row virtualization. Columns: checkbox · Monitor (status ring + name) · IP · Type (product type icons) · Status (status tag). Header sortable; search box on top; selected-count badge + View-All/View-Selected toggles.

icon-dot / severity dropdown.useWhen: each option needs a leading GLYPH to be recognised — a severity colour dot, a monitor-type icon, a status colour — shown both per-option and in the collapsed trigger.
icon-dot / severity dropdown.dontUse: plain text options (use the basic dropdown). If the glyph needs a whole column of context, use the grid dropdown.
icon-dot / severity dropdown.example: severity-picker (colour dot per severity), monitor-type picker (type icon), status pickers — via the before-menu-text (and after-menu-text) slot. 27 files.

tree-select (hierarchy).useWhen: the choices are HIERARCHICAL (parent → children) and the user navigates by expanding nodes — the codebase has no cascader, this is its equivalent.
tree-select (hierarchy).dontUse: a flat list (basic dropdown) or a multi-column record picker (grid dropdown).
tree-select (hierarchy).example: monitor-hierarchy-picker — Data Centers → sites → monitors, expand/collapse with counts; a leaf is selectable.

avatar / people picker.useWhen: the options are PEOPLE — show an avatar (initials/photo) + name so the user is recognised at a glance.
avatar / people picker.dontUse: non-user options. For bulk user assignment across many columns, use the grid-table mode of user-picker.
avatar / people picker.example: owner / assignee / approver / notified-user selection (user-picker.vue, dual list + grid modes).

virtualized rich-row list.useWhen: each option is a multi-line CARD (title + meta + glyph) and there can be many — the menu virtualizes tall rows instead of single-line options.
virtualized rich-row list.example: notification dropdown (alert cards), widget selector (thumbnails), counter list. 16 files, RecycleScroller.

trigger: button.useWhen: the opener is a labelled action

column-chooser.useWhen: a table lets users show/hide (and reorder) columns.
column-chooser.dontUse: a general value picker (the default select).
column-chooser.example: columns=[{key,label,checked?,locked?}] heading="COLUMNS" reset-label="Reset Column Preference" — opens from an eye button.

knownIssues: F1 (high, a11y) -> promoted to SF-003: not an accessible combobox — no role/aria-expanded/activedescendant, click-only open (not keyboard-openable), no focus ring (SF-001). Highest-impact a11y gap (510x). See findings/SF-003.
F2 (medium): maxAllowedSelection declared but never used; real cap is maxValues. Consumers (LooseTags asDropdown) pass it expecting a limit.
F3 (low): searchable/asInput/wrap default to true (against vue/no-boolean-default).
F4 (low): loose option schema (text||name||label, key||id||value). Document canonical { key, text }.
SB caveat (tooling): search needs the arrayWorker web worker (no-op in Storybook); no-data SVG needs an svg-component loader (absent in SB).

[product bug, FIXED] .dropdown-trigger-input input.ant-input used the padding shorthand with vertical/horizontal SWAPPED (padding: 11px-horizontal 4px-vertical => CSS reads it as 11px vertical + 4px left, tight and mis-centered). Fixed all 4 occurrences in src/design/dropdown.less to the correct order (4px vertical / 11px left = standard input). The same swap remains in src/design/input.less:351 (.rounded-background input) — flagged for owner review, broader scope.

changelog.change: Added the COLUMN-CHOOSER variant to the Dropdown (obs-select): a `columns` prop renders a COLUMNS header + draggable checkbox rows (drag-reorder via a 6-dot grip; locked columns pinned) + a Reset footer, opened from an eye icon trigger. Emits change/reorder/reset. Replaces the briefly-separate obs-column-chooser (folded into the Dropdown, per owner).

changelog: 2026-07-14: Group B shipped on obs-select (owner) — the previously-documented-but-unbuilt variants are now real element features, modelled as TWO orthogonal axes + route-aways (not N components): (A) OPTION CONTENT — rich options render `icon`→obs-icon, `severity`(or a --severity color)→obs-severity dot, `avatar`+`sublabel/email`→a people row (this also fixed the old reuse violations: the option icon was v-html raw HTML and the dot was a hand-drawn span). (B) TRIGGER — a `trigger` enum input|text|button|icon|chip (button + icon are new; icon shows a multi-select count badge). (C) TREE-SELECT — options with nested `children[]` render a real N-level hierarchy (flattened list, per-level indent, expand/collapse chevron; branch checkbox = subtree select with indeterminate). ROUTE-AWAYS: multi-COLUMN rich rows / 'virtualized rich-row list' are obs-grid-select (composes obs-table), not this — a columnless rich list is option content here. Plain + one-level-group selects verified byte-identical (regression).

2026-07-11: added a decisionFlow ROUTE-AWAY to obs-grid-select — 'picking a rich record identified by multiple columns (name/IP/type/status), often multi-select? -> Grid Select, not this'. grid-select shipped as its own top-level component (its menu is a searchable table, not an option list), so an AI tool matching that use-case now resolves to it directly instead of a plain dropdown; the two registries cross-route both ways.

2026-06-07: added — full deep-dive of _base-dropdown-picker + dropdown-trigger family (510x/241 files); rendered real default mode in SB via v-tooltip/MPopper/RecycleScroller registration; F1-F4 + SB caveats.

2026-07-10: catalogued the GRID / TABLE dropdown variant (FlotoDropdownGridSelector + MonitorPicker/AgentPicker) — the "Select Agent/Monitor" table picker (~70×). Added the Storybook GridDropdown story (render-faithful reproduction with the real MStatusTag + product icons + .ds-grid chrome) + usageRule (when to use a grid picker vs a plain dropdown vs an action menu). One of 5 Group-A dropdown variants the product sweep found missing.

2026-07-10: grid-dropdown — added the selected-state affordances the first pass missed (owner-caught): a selected-count BADGE + View Selected/View All toggle + Clear Selected links appear beside the search when rows are checked, and a checked row gets the selected highlight + left accent (ds-grid-row-selected).

2026-07-10: grid-dropdown polish (owner-caught): TYPE cell white-gap fixed (a flex <td> lost display:table-cell so the selected-row bg did not fill — moved flex to an inner span); View Selected/Clear Selected restyled to navy underlined + light divider; the trigger now REFLECTS the selection (selected name / name +N) instead of the static placeholder; the search box is the REUSED product MInput (was a hand-rolled input).

2026-07-10: catalogued the remaining 4 Group-A dropdown variants (Storybook stories + usageRules): icon/severity-dot (before-menu-text, 27×), tree-select (monitor-hierarchy, the cascader equivalent), avatar/people picker (user-picker), and virtualized rich-row list (notification/widget, 16×). With the grid dropdown, all 5 Group-A missed variants from the product sweep are now in the DS.

2026-07-10: Group-A polish (owner-caught): grid — reduced the search↔actions gap (fixed-width search, not flex:1) and gave View/Clear Selected the product LINK treatment (dotted underline, per _base-app-link, not solid); tree — every PARENT node now shows a deep-dive chevron (inline SVG + rotate, incl. collapsed nodes); avatar — trigger gap between the initials circle and the name (via before-menu-text nbsp, since the .ant-tag trigger resets slot margins).

2026-07-10: avatar picker trigger overlap fixed (root cause): the trigger is an Ant input with a position:absolute prefix; its default padding-left was too small for the 22px avatar so the name overlapped it. Widened the input padding (a <style> in a Vue template is stripped; set via a mounted hook + !important + retry since the picker re-renders).

2026-07-10: documented the TRIGGER AXIS (Group B) — the trigger slot ({ toggle }) opens the SAME menu via input / text-only / button / icon-only / chip (130× via v-slot:trigger). Added a Triggers Storybook story + a triggers{} block + usageRules so AI tools pick the right opener independent of the menu content.

2026-07-11: fixed a product CSS bug (owner-found via inspect): the dropdown trigger input padding shorthand had vertical/horizontal SWAPPED (padding: 11px 4px → should be 4px 11px). Corrected all 4 occurrences in src/design/dropdown.less; the input now has standard 4px vertical / 11px left padding. Same swap noted in input.less:351 (broader, flagged for review).

a11y.summary: Once open: ↑/↓ move the active row, Enter selects, Esc closes.
issues: Opens on click only — no Enter/Space/↓ on the trigger.
a11y.$note: Catalogue-wide gap SF-001 = no visible :focus-visible ring; tracked in findings/.
